data.gender_notes: Marek is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic name Mar, which comes from Mars, the Roman god of war. In Christianity, Marek may symbolize strength, courage, and protection. The name Marek carries the meaning “Mars' warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Marek usually hope their child will grow to embody mars' warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: מרק
in_hebrew.meaning: מרק הוא שם שפירושו ביטוי מריר או ירק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מרק נגזר מהשורש העברי 'מרק' שפירושו ביטוי מריר או ירק, ויש לו קשרים עם המילה 'מרור' שפירושו מר. השם מרק מופיע בתנ"ך כמרקוס, שם של מחבר הבשורה על פי מרקוס.

in_greek.name: Μαρκ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαρκ προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'Μάρκος' που σημαίνει 'πικρός' ή 'Martyr'. Ο Μαρκ είναι σύντομη μορφή του ονόματος Μάρκος που αναφέρεται στο Ευαγγέλιο του Μάρκου.

in_latin.name: Marek
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Marek is derived from the Latin 'Marcus', which means 'bitter' or 'Martyr'. It is related to the Greek name 'Μάρκος' (Markos) and has been used in Christian tradition to signify a person of strong faith.

in_english.name: Marek
in_english.meaning: Marek means bitter or Martyr in Christian tradition
in_english.long_meaning: The name Marek originates from the Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning 'bitter' or 'Martyr'. It is associated with Saint Mark, the author of the Gospel of Mark in the New Testament. Marek symbolizes strength and devotion in Christian faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Marek has been widely used among the Slavic peoples, particularly in regions such as Poland, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic. Historically, the name has been associated with warriors and rulers, reflecting the influence of Ancient Roman culture on the early Slavic societies. Additionally, the name has strong ties to the Catholic Church, as Saint Marcellinus and Saint Mark, who was the evangelist and writer of the New Testament, are both popular saints with the name Mar.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, Marek may symbolize strength, courage, and protection. Named after the Roman god of war, this name carries associations with heroism, bravery, and fearlessness, all of which are essential virtues for a Christian. Furthermore, the name coincides with several religious figures, most notably Saint Mark the Evangelist, who is believed to have brought Christianity to the Slavic peoples. This further cements the spiritual significance of the name Marek, representing a powerful connection between one's spiritual beliefs and their personal identity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Marek, meaning "rebel" or "warlike" in Slavic origin, symbolizes the rebellious spirit of St. Mark the Evangelist, who boldly proclaimed the gospel message against all odds. In a more spiritual sense, it represents the inner strength and courage to stand up for one's faith in the face of adversity.

biblical_reference.note: The Gospel of Mark is one of the four canonical Gospels in the New Testament.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Mark the Evangelist, also known as Mark the Apostle or Mark the Elder, was the author of the second Gospel. He is believed to have been a companion of Saint Peter and traveled with him to Rome in the 1st century AD. According to tradition, Mark's gospel was written to provide an account for those who had not heard the teachings of Jesus in person, and to help those who had heard Peter's preaching to commit these teachings to memory.
historical_references.context: Legendary account of the authorship of the second Gospel

historical_references.reference: Mark the Evangelist is also identified with Mark of Cyrene, who according to the New Testament, was forced to carry the cross of Jesus during his Passion. This identification is not accepted by all scholars, as it is not mentioned in the earliest accounts of the Passion.
historical_references.context: New Testament reference to Mark the Evangelist
